sources.name: GUGiK ULDK national parcel lookup (Usługa Lokalizacji Działek Katastralnych)
sources.scope: National point and exact-ID lookup of EGiB cadastral parcels (one parcel per request, WGS84 output requested from the provider). Live-verified on 2026-10-12 for 51 of 53 uncovered Polish UN cities (point containment, identical exact re-read, explicit absence). Earlier live samples: Warsaw and Kraków (2026-09-29), Bydgoszcz (2026-10-09). Bbox queries and area enumeration are unavailable.
caveats: Point and exact-ID lookup only: a clicked parcel never proves a viewport complete.
ULDK serves EGiB data held by county starosties; counties whose data is missing, stale or temporarily unavailable may answer with the same no-result line as a genuinely absent parcel.
Explicit absence is accepted only from the exact reply "-1 brak wyników"; every other "-1" message, count line, HTML or non-text reply is treated as unavailable.
Parcel IDs outside the documented TERYT form WWPPGG_R.OOOO[.AR_N].NR_DZ are rejected rather than coerced; unusual county numbering would surface as provider errors, not silent data.
Geometry is the provider's own EPSG:2180 to EPSG:4326 output, unrounded and unrepaired; the adapter rejects any returned polygon that does not contain the queried point.
Requests are paced to one start per second per adapter instance; GUGiK publishes no rate limit.

knownLimit.evidence: 2026-10-12: from one consumer network GUGiK host names failed to resolve (SERVFAIL) and connections to the resolved address timed out, while the production relay and another server got answers. Which networks are affected is unpublished.

sources.operator: Główny Urząd Geodezji i Kartografii (GUGiK); EGiB data maintained by county starosties
sources.attribution: GUGiK ULDK · county EGiB cadastral parcels · parcel lookup on click
sources.licenceNote: Anonymous public HTTPS API without credentials. ULDK's own reuse terms were not read in this session (documentation host unreachable from the verification machine); confirm them before publication. Cadastral geometry does not establish legal title or survey accuracy.

jurisdiction.basis: ULDK is GUGiK's national parcel lookup that answers point and TERYT-ID queries from the county EGiB cadastral databases.

sources.name: GUGiK collective EGiB WFS (Zbiorcza usługa WFS EGiB) — county cadastral parcels
sources.operator: Główny Urząd Geodezji i Kartografii (GUGiK); EGiB data maintained by county starosties
sources.scope: Poland: GUGiK's collective WFS of county EGiB cadastral parcels (launched 2026-07-16). It holds the counties whose own WFS is listed in EZiUDP; a county missing there is missing here, so each city is qualified separately. Requested fields are the TERYT parcel ID and geometry only.
caveats: A collective of county services: a county's data is as current as its own service, and a county absent from the collective returns no parcels.

One page states the whole set's numberMatched when the set fits (pages of up to 500, about 3 s each), so a cell or a 3x3 block of cells is usually one request; larger or empty sets use hits, pages and hits.
Geometry is the provider's EPSG:2180 output (northing, easting) reprojected to WGS84 unrepaired; parcel IDs equal ULDK's TERYT IDs.
No CORS headers: browsers read it through the production provider relay.
sources.attribution: GUGiK collective EGiB WFS · county cadastral parcels · adapted
sources.licenceNote: GetCapabilities declares Fees none and AccessConstraints none. Public EGiB WFS services carry only data provided free of charge (art. 40a(2) of the Polish Geodetic and Cartographic Law, as summarised by GUGiK). Cadastral geometry does not establish legal title or survey accuracy.

jurisdiction.basis: GUGiK's collective WFS gathers the county EGiB cadastral parcel services listed in EZiUDP into one national layer.

sources.operator: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE), ArcGIS Online public view of a statewide county-parcel compilation
sources.scope: Statewide California county-parcel compilation (58 county FIPS codes present, 13,138,000 rows on 2026-10-12). Canonical identity is the county FIPS code plus the county assessor parcel number; the 23,032 rows without an APN are outside this source.
caveats: APNs are county-scoped number spaces, so identity is the reversible composite FIPS_CODE~PARCEL_APN; PARCEL_DMP_ID (an aggregator key with several batch prefixes) is not used.

Condominium-style rows repeat one APN with byte-identical lot geometry (e.g. 582 rows for one Los Angeles APN); the adapter keeps one polygon per APN. No APN with differing Shape__Area was found in Los Angeles, Sacramento, Orange or Contra Costa counties; a differing repeat elsewhere fails closed.
Distinct APNs can share one identical lot polygon (observed in Orange and Contra Costa bbox samples).
metricSrid 32611 suits southern California; cities west of 120 W need a per-city metric projection (e.g. 32610) when qualified.
Layer derives from a statewide compilation of county data (data last edited 2026-05-28); per-county currency was not established and no licence text is published in the service metadata.
sources.attribution: CAL FIRE, California Statewide Parcels Public View (county assessor parcel data). Adapted to WGS84.
sources.licenceNote: Source conditions are informational; users choose their source and intended use.

jurisdiction.basis: CAL FIRE publishes this layer as California statewide parcels; all 58 county FIPS codes are present in the live layer.

sources.name: Florida Statewide Cadastral (Department of Revenue)
sources.operator: Florida Department of Revenue, Property Tax Oversight, from the 67 county property appraisers
sources.scope: Florida DOR statewide cadastral polygons joined to the county tax rolls for all 67 counties (10,950,718 rows on 2026-10-12). Canonical identity is the DOR county number plus roll PARCEL_ID; same-key rows form one native parcel group. The 97,244 polygons with no roll join (CO_NO 0, blank PARCEL_ID) are outside this source.
caveats: PARCEL_ID is county-scoped, so identity is the reversible composite CO_NO~PARCEL_ID.

Many roll parcels are stored as several polygon rows (e.g. 86 rows for one Hillsborough condominium parcel); all components are fetched and unioned. Some components overlap slightly (largest observed 0.79 m2), so overlap is not rejected for this provider.
The layer carries owner, address and sale columns; only CO_NO, PARCEL_ID and OBJECTID are requested.
Statewide envelope queries are slow (about 11 s for a 0.01 degree box, 18 s for 46 object IDs); small cells are required.
sources.attribution: Florida Department of Revenue, Property Tax Oversight, and Florida county property appraisers. Adapted to WGS84.
sources.licenceNote: Source conditions are informational; users choose their source and intended use.

jurisdiction.basis: The DOR layer is collected annually from all 67 Florida county property appraisers; all 67 county numbers are present in the live layer.

sources.name: Massachusetts Property Tax Parcels (MassGIS Level 3)
sources.operator: MassGIS (Bureau of Geographic Information), Commonwealth of Massachusetts
sources.scope: MassGIS Level 3 standardized assessor parcel polygons for all 351 Massachusetts cities and towns (2,559,636 rows on 2026-10-12), identified by the MassGIS LOC_ID locational parcel identifier. All published POLY_TYPE values are included; the one row without a LOC_ID is excluded.
caveats: The layer joins polygons to assessing records, so one LOC_ID repeats once per assessing record with byte-identical geometry (up to 865 rows in Boston); the adapter keeps one polygon per LOC_ID. No LOC_ID with differing Shape__Area was found in Boston, Worcester or Springfield.
MAP_PAR_ID is a town-scoped assessor map-parcel label used only for display; it is blank on some polygons.
Non-FEE polygon types (TAX 63,180, PRIV_ROW 832, RAIL_ROW 530, ROW 232, WATER 73 rows) are included; sampled TAX, PRIV_ROW and WATER polygons did not overlap FEE polygons.
Publisher text: standardization is complete for 350 of 351 communities and Boston is processed separately; Boston (TOWN_ID 35) rows are present in this layer.
metricSrid 32619 suits eastern Massachusetts; cities west of 72 W (e.g. Springfield) need 32618 when qualified.
sources.attribution: MassGIS (Bureau of Geographic Information), Commonwealth of Massachusetts. Adapted to WGS84.
sources.licenceNote: Source conditions are informational; users choose their source and intended use.

jurisdiction.basis: MassGIS documents Level 3 assessor parcels for every Massachusetts community; all 351 TOWN_ID values are present in the live layer.

sources.name: Ohio Statewide Parcels (OGRIP)
sources.operator: Ohio Geographically Referenced Information Program (OGRIP), Ohio Department of Administrative Services, from county auditor parcel data
sources.scope: OGRIP statewide compilation of county auditor parcels for all 88 Ohio counties (6,313,610 rows on 2026-10-12). Canonical identity is County plus the county LocalParcelID; same-key rows form one native parcel group. Rows with a null, empty or single-space LocalParcelID are excluded.
caveats: StateParcelID (39 + county FIPS + LocalParcelID) is published but the service rejects every SQL predicate on it (HTTP 200 error 400), so the equivalent County~LocalParcelID composite is used.

Some counties publish one LocalParcelID on several polygons (13 IDs in Franklin, 67 in Hamilton); all components are fetched and unioned. Byte-identical copies of a component also repeat, so disjointParts is off (with it on, Hamilton 0940008042100 failed); sampled distinct components did not overlap.
Hamilton County stacks byte-identical condominium polygons under distinct LocalParcelIDs (31 shared polygons in one 0.01 degree Cincinnati box).

About 25,000 rows carry no usable LocalParcelID (e.g. 5,664 null in Franklin, 1,709 single-space in Hamilton) and are outside this source; a few counties put free-text notes in LocalParcelID, which are kept verbatim.
metricSrid 32617 suits central/eastern Ohio; cities west of 84 W (e.g. Cincinnati, Dayton) need 32616 when qualified.
sources.attribution: Ohio Geographically Referenced Information Program (OGRIP) and Ohio county auditors. Adapted to WGS84.
sources.licenceNote: Source conditions are informational; users choose their source and intended use.

jurisdiction.basis: OGRIP compiles county auditor parcels into one statewide layer; all 88 Ohio counties are present in the live layer.

sources.name: Colorado Public Parcels (OIT statewide composite)
sources.operator: Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology (OIT) GIS, from county and municipal parcel data
sources.scope: OIT statewide composite of 44 of 64 Colorado counties (2,600,023 rows on 2026-10-12). Canonical identity is countyName plus the county parcel_id; same-key rows form one native parcel group. Rows without parcel_id (5,310) are excluded.
caveats: Absent counties: Alamosa, Baca, Bent, Chaffee, Cheyenne, Conejos, Costilla, Crowley, Delta, Fremont, Jackson, Kiowa, Kit Carson, Las Animas, Lincoln, Mineral, Montrose, Otero, Phillips, Prowers.
parcel_id is county-scoped (the Denver entry fixes countyName for this reason), so identity is the composite countyName~parcel_id.

Larimer (1,133 IDs) and Boulder (834 IDs) publish one parcel_id on several polygons plus stacked byte-identical copies (up to 487 rows); all components are fetched and unioned. disjointParts is off because stacked copies fail the overlap check (Boulder 146329311017 failed with it on); sampled distinct components did not overlap.
Distinct parcel_ids can share one identical polygon (stacked condominium units; 25 shared polygons in one 0.01 degree Fort Collins box).
sources.attribution: Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology GIS and contributing counties. Adapted to WGS84.
sources.licenceNote: Source conditions are informational; users choose their source and intended use.

jurisdiction.basis: OIT aggregates county and municipal parcels into one statewide layer, but only 44 of 64 counties are present; cities in the 20 absent counties cannot qualify.

sources.name: NCSCM CZMP 2019 — Maharashtra survey plots
sources.scope: Survey-plot outlines drawn on Maharashtra's Coastal Zone Management Plan 2019 maps, including city survey (CTS) and town-planning-scheme (TPS) plots in Greater Mumbai. Coverage follows mapped coastal planning areas and can omit inland neighbourhoods. Labels repeat within a village, so application references are derived from each outline and change when an outline changes.
sources.attribution: National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management (MoEFCC) — CZMP 2019 survey plots, Maharashtra. Plot labels shown as published; references derived from geometry. Adapted to WGS84.
sources.licenceNote: No reuse licence is stated on the CZMP portal or the ArcGIS service; the plan is published for public viewing.
caveats: Coastal-zone planning maps, not the land-records register: plot outlines are a geometry reference, not proof of current title or ownership.
The layer mixes CTS and TPS plots. VILLAGE + TYPE + label repeats for distinct polygons, so it is shown, never used as identity; OBJECTID is a transport field.

Application identity uses the source namespace plus canonical geometry SHA-256 at 1e-7-degree precision and a spatial locator, as for Nairobi. A changed outline gets a new reference; absence means that outline version was not returned.
The service answers browsers directly (CORS allows this site); no relay is used.
The plan dates from the CRZ Notification 2019; the survey date of the underlying plot maps is not stated.

sources.name: Matribhoomi (Survey of India) — Chapra tehsil cadastral map, Bihar (overlaps resolved)
sources.scope: Khesra parcels of Chapra tehsil (Bihar) on the national Matribhoomi cadastral map service, keyed by the village map code (BHUCODE), khesra number and part. Parcel types include agricultural plots, settlement (abadi), roads and water.
sources.attribution: Matribhoomi cadastral map service (Government of India, mapservice.gov.in) — Bihar village maps. Adapted to WGS84.
sources.licenceNote: No reuse licence is stated on the public Matribhoomi map service.
caveats: Village cadastral maps: not proof of current title or ownership.
OBJECTID is a transport field; identity is BHUCODE + KID + KPARTH (a blank part is kept as published).

Some outlines overlap (neighbouring village maps were drawn and georeferenced separately). Each overlap is given to the larger outline (equal areas: the lower reference); the smaller parcel shows the rest as derived ground. References still come from the published outline or key.
Found through ramSeraph/indian_cadastrals (github.com/ramSeraph/indian_cadastrals); the map is read live from mapservice.gov.in.
The service answers browsers directly (CORS allows this site); no relay is used.
The server's certificate chains to Let's Encrypt's ISRG Root YR, which current Chrome trusts but older systems and Node's bundled store may not.

Found through ramSeraph/indian_cadastrals (github.com/ramSeraph/indian_cadastrals), which lists HSAC as an original source; the map is read live from HSAC.

identity.recipe: Lowercase SHA-256 of the unchanged little-endian SHP geometry record content, excluding its 8-byte record framing. This includes geometry type, source-derived bbox, ring indices and every native double coordinate, with no row number or byte offset in the identity. Prefix with source ID + /native-shape-sha256-v1/. Identical native geometries deduplicate; source corrections/reordering of coordinates change references.
identity.reason: Native ID repeats across sheets; geometry-derived references avoid reading any DBF attributes. These are source geometry references, not legal parcel identifiers.

identity.recipe: Lowercase SHA-256 of the unchanged little-endian SHP geometry record content, excluding its 8-byte record framing.
